questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Morocco?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Morocco article.

questions.proof: The capital of Morocco is Rabat.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Morocco?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Morocco on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Morocco article.

questions.proof: Morocco is next to the countries of Algeria to its east, Mauritania to its south and Spain and Portugal as well as the United Kingdom at Gibraltar.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Morocco?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People and culture” part of the Morocco article.

questions.proof: Moroccans are an Arabic speaking ethnic group of mixed Berber and European descent.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Spain also occupied parts of Morocco before leaving them in _____ and in 1975.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Morocco article, under the heading “People and culture”.

questions.proof: Spain also occupied parts of Morocco before leaving them in 1956 and in 1975.
